title: Interface vs Type Alias in TypeScript

scenes.say: Ever wonder when to use an interface versus a type alias in TypeScript? Let's clear it up.
Interfaces describe object shapes and can be extended or merged. Type aliases are more flexible—they handle unions, primitives, and tuples, but can't be merged.
Here's the cool part: interfaces with the same name get merged. Add a property later, and TypeScript combines them automatically.

scenes.label: Best Use
scenes.sub: Use interface for extensible objects, type for unions or primitives.
scenes.say: My rule: use interfaces for objects you'll extend, and type aliases for unions or primitives.

scenes.question: Can type aliases be merged?
scenes.right: No, only interfaces support merging. Type aliases can't be combined.
scenes.say: Watch out: only interfaces support merging. Type aliases can't be combined, so don't mix them up in interviews.
